name: Micro Open/Close Module
description: A small in-box module that controls 110 V motorized devices such as projection screens, shutters, and curtains. It supports several switch types and has adjustable open and close travel times.

steps.text: Write down the Insteon ID printed on the back of the module.
Turn off the breaker or fuse and verify that the power is off.
Disconnect the wires from the existing switch, fixture or outlet and strip 3/16 inch (5 mm) of bare wire on each end.
Connect the wires following the wiring diagram for your installation; sense wire 1 (yellow) is up and sense wire 2 (purple) is down.
Make sure the wires are firm and no bare wire is exposed, then turn on the breaker or fuse.
steps.expect: After a few seconds the LED turns green

steps.text: Test by tapping the module's up and down buttons.
steps.expect: Motor moves; LED green when moving up/open, red when moving down/closed

steps.text: If wired behind a single or dual momentary switch, set the switch operation mode: press and hold the SET button until it beeps three times in turn (LED blinks green, red, green), slowly tap it four times for single momentary or five for dual momentary, then press and hold it until it double-beeps.

Calibrate the travel time: press and hold the SET button until it beeps four times in turn (LED blinks green, red, green, red), slowly tap it twice, press and hold it until it beeps (the motor starts), tap it as soon as the load is fully lowered or raised (the motor reverses), and tap it again when fully raised or lowered.

notes: Determine the switch type first (latching, the default; single momentary; or dual momentary); switch operation mode doesn't apply when installed behind an outlet or in a fixture.
Stay with the module during calibration; your taps set the timing.
Sense wires carry very low current (about 0.17 mA at 120 V, 0.35 mA at 240 V).

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.

notes: As controller: adjust the responder to the state you want, then press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps. The module double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.

Instead of the SET button you can quickly tap the connected wall switch exactly five times in under four seconds (alternate directions on a latching or dual momentary switch), then wait two seconds; the module beeps.
As responder: put the controller in linking mode, move the load up or down to the state you want, then press and hold the module's SET button (or tap the switch five times) until it double-beeps.
Do the SET button steps before reinstalling the wall switch or fixture.
If either device's LED keeps blinking, the link failed; tap its SET button until the LED stops and try again.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request; the device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version.

Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping a few times to check the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, and the device's group 1 to the Hub as a controller.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.
Once linked, the Hub reads the device's settings with Get Operating Flags and an extended Get for group 1.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
Tap the SET button.
For each responder, adjust it to the scene state and press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps.
Tap the SET button to finish.
Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again until it beeps.

notes: Then press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps; the module double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.
To unlink several responders, tap the SET button after the LED blinks red (it double-blinks red), press and hold each responder's SET button until it double-beeps, then tap the SET button to finish.

To remove the module as a responder, put the controller in unlinking mode (hold its button until it beeps, then again until it beeps and its LED blinks red) and press and hold the module's SET button until it double-beeps.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again until it beeps.
Press and hold the SET button a third time until it beeps.
Slowly tap the SET button 3 times.
Press and hold the SET button and don't let go.
When the beep stops, release the SET button.
steps.expect: After a few seconds, a double beep

notes: Erases all settings, links and scenes.

steps.text: Remove the module as a controller from each of its responders.
Remove all of the module's responder links from its controllers.

notes: Otherwise controllers keep retrying commands and cause network delays.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene on the Hub first.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder, for group 0; the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09), as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: The Hub won't remove a device that still belongs to a scene.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.
